title: First Passage Time via csInf Theory

problemStatement.formal: fpt_le_iff_maxEvent : ∀ (bm : BrownianMotion Ω μ) (a T : ℝ), 0 < T → (∀ ω, bm.path · ω |>.Continuous) → ∀ ω, firstPassageTime bm a ω ≤ T ↔ ω ∈ maxEvent bm a T
problemStatement.plain: The parent BallotProblemOQ02.lean axiomatizes firstPassageTime_eq_maxEvent: {ω | τ(ω) ≤ T} = maxEvent bm a T. Can this be proved from path continuity and csInf theory? We prove both directions under natural hypotheses, characterize when the parent axiom holds (when the hitting set is nonempty), and use IVT to show that if W(T,ω) ≥ a then there is a first crossing in (0,T].
whyMatters: Proves the parent axiom firstPassageTime_eq_maxEvent holds under the nonemptiness hypothesis
Reveals a subtle gap: sInf ∅ = 0 in Lean's ℝ, so the unrestricted axiom is false without nonemptiness
Applies the Intermediate Value Theorem to Brownian paths for the backward direction

proven: hittingSet_isClosed: {t ≥ 0 | W(t,ω) ≥ a} is closed (from path continuity)
hittingSet_bddBelow: the hitting set is bounded below by 0
hittingSet_csInf_mem: if hitting set is nonempty, csInf is a member (from closedness)
ivt_first_crossing: if W(0,ω) < a ≤ W(T,ω), there exists t ∈ (0,T] with W(t,ω) ≥ a
hittingSet_nonempty_of_ivt: IVT gives nonempty hitting set
fpt_le_T_of_crossing: first passage time ≤ T when IVT crossing occurs
